original_idea: O nosso clube de leitura recebe poucos lugares para encontros presenciais e temos de decidir quem participa quando há mais interessados do que vagas. Não quero que vire uma disputa por rapidez de inscrição, mas também não sei qual critério seria justo para todos.
current_idea: Implement a fixed rotating schedule with a shared calendar and limited sign‑up windows, complemented by a randomized weighted lottery per cycle to allocate spots fairly.
human_intent: Find a fair criterion for selecting participants that does not turn into a race based on rapid sign‑up and is acceptable to all members.
problem_statement: The reading club has limited in‑person meeting spots, leading to a situation where more members want to attend than there are available places, creating a need for a fair allocation method.
assumptions: The number of available seats is fixed and smaller than the number of interested members
All members want equal opportunity to attend
No existing formal selection criteria are in place
Members value fairness over speed of registration
Meetings occur regularly enough to consider rotating attendance
ambiguities: What specific definition of "fair" the members expect (e.g., random, seniority, contribution)
Whether members can attend multiple meetings or only one per cycle
How often the allocation method should be refreshed or rotated
If any members have special needs or priorities that affect selection
strengths: The problem is clearly identified: limited spots vs. excess demand
The intent to avoid a speed‑based competition is explicitly stated
The desire for a universally acceptable solution suggests openness to various fair mechanisms

critical_issues.issue: Absence of a concrete allocation algorithm
critical_issues.why_it_matters: Without a defined mechanism (e.g., lottery, rotating schedule, points system) the club cannot implement the promised fairness, leading to ad‑hoc decisions that may be perceived as biased.

critical_issues.issue: Potential for perceived inequity in rotating attendance
critical_issues.why_it_matters: Rotating spots assumes equal interest over time, but members may have varying availability or desire to attend specific sessions, causing dissatisfaction and possible attrition.

fragile_assumptions: All members want equal opportunity to attend
Members value fairness over speed of registration
Meetings occur regularly enough to consider rotating attendance
The number of available seats is fixed and smaller than the number of interested members
No existing informal selection practices are in place
contradictions: The desire to avoid a race based on quick registration conflicts with the need for a deterministic rule that can be applied quickly
Assuming no existing criteria while members may already have informal expectations about who gets spots
failure_modes: Members lose trust if the chosen method is seen as arbitrary or manipulable
Repeated exclusion of the same members leads to reduced participation and club vitality
Lack of transparency in the selection process creates disputes and factionalism

alternatives.mechanism: Randomized weighted lottery per cycle, where each member receives a number of tickets proportional to how many times they have attended recently; a computer draws the winners for each sign‑up window
addresses_issues: Absence of a concrete allocation algorithm
Potential for perceived inequity in rotating attendance
tradeoffs: Introduces randomness that some may view as less predictable
Requires tracking of past attendance and a fair random number generator
May be perceived as unfair by members who prefer deterministic order
alternatives.novelty_or_difference: Combines probabilistic fairness with historical attendance weighting to break pure rotation patterns

alternatives.mechanism: Points‑based credit system: members earn credits each time they attend a meeting and spend credits to secure a spot in upcoming sign‑up windows; the schedule still rotates but priority is given to those with higher credit balances
addresses_issues: Absence of a concrete allocation algorithm
Potential for perceived inequity in rotating attendance
tradeoffs: Adds administrative overhead to track and update credit balances
May incentivize over‑attendance, creating burnout risk
Potential for gaming the system if credits are not carefully managed
alternatives.novelty_or_difference: Introduces a gamified, merit‑based layer on top of the rotating schedule, turning fairness into a transparent economy

alternatives.mechanism: Blockchain‑backed smart contract that enforces a deterministic round‑robin allocation with cryptographic timestamps; each sign‑up window is recorded immutably, and the contract automatically rejects entries that would break the rotation
addresses_issues: Absence of a concrete allocation algorithm
Potential for perceived inequity in rotating attendance
tradeoffs: Requires technical expertise and infrastructure to deploy and maintain the smart contract
Members must learn to interact with the blockchain interface
Potential latency or cost issues depending on the chosen platform
alternatives.novelty_or_difference: Leverages decentralized ledger technology to provide an immutable, transparent allocation mechanism that eliminates doubts about fairness

core_mechanism: Fixed rotating schedule with shared calendar and limited sign‑up windows
core_mechanism_justification: Ensures each member gets a predictable turn while preventing race conditions; aligns directly with the user's desire for a fair, non‑racing allocation.

known_risks: Perception that randomness may be unfair despite weighting.
Administrative overhead to maintain attendance records and ticket counts.
Potential for members to game the lottery if ticket allocation rules are not clear.
recommended_next_step: Run a pilot cycle using the rotating schedule with limited sign‑up windows and the weighted lottery, monitor member feedback, and refine the ticket allocation rules before full rollout.
tested_core_mechanism: Fixed rotating schedule with shared calendar and limited sign‑up windows
reality_dependencies: A shared digital calendar platform that all members can access and edit
Automated notification system (email or push) to alert members when their sign‑up window opens and closes
Agreement among members on the length of each sign‑up window and the rotation order
Reliable time‑zone handling to ensure all members see the same window times
Procedures for handling missed sign‑ups (e.g., automatic pass‑over to next member)
claims_needing_evidence: A fixed rotating schedule eliminates the incentive for rapid sign‑up races
Limited sign‑up windows reduce the occurrence of last‑minute overbooking
The combined system provides a perception of fairness comparable to random lottery methods
candidate_tests: Run a controlled simulation of two full rotation cycles with a representative group of members and record sign‑up timestamps to verify that no member signs up outside their allocated window
Introduce a deliberate missed sign‑up and observe whether the system correctly passes the slot to the next member in the rotation
Measure the distribution of sign‑up attempts before and after implementing limited windows to confirm a reduction in peak sign‑up traffic
Survey participants after a trial period to assess perceived fairness versus the previous lottery approach
exploratory_candidate_tests: Prototype a points‑based credit system layered on top of the rotating schedule and test whether credit accumulation influences spot allocation without breaking rotation integrity
Develop a blockchain smart‑contract prototype that records sign‑up windows and enforces round‑robin allocation; evaluate its performance and usability compared to the calendar‑based implementation
